task: Prime-dimensional Weyl self-compatibility versus factor-two entanglement-breaking domination

claims.statement: For prime d, the factor-two mode inequalities are feasible within the convex hull of the d+1 maximal-abelian line-dephasing channels and the depolarizing channel if and only if B(lambda)=sum_L max_{x in L\{0}} (2 lambda_x-1)_+ is at most 1.
claims.quantifiers: Any real Weyl-diagonal spectrum; necessary and sufficient only for this specified mixture ansatz.
claims.proof: Each nonzero phase-space mode lies on one unique projective line. A mixture has eigenvalue w_L on that line, so all inequalities hold iff w_L is at least the maximum clipped target on L and the sum of required weights is at most one.
claims.boundary: B>1 rules out the line-dephasing mixture only; it is not a separability or general EB obstruction.

claims.statement: There is an exact d=5 unital CPTP, Hilbert-Schmidt-self-adjoint Weyl-covariant channel with a two-output CPTP extension and line-cover budget B=(6294997/6303442)+(476808 sqrt(5)/3151721)>1.
claims.quantifiers: One fixed channel in dimension five; all its Weyl modes are specified by four exact Q(sqrt(5)) classes in FINAL_REPORT.md.
claims.proof_core: The class vector f is fixed by the normalized symplectic Fourier transform. The kernel X=f f^T/N is PSD, has diagonal q=f^2/N, and its compatibility transform is q again. Haapasalo's finite-Weyl criterion therefore yields a two-output extension. Exact mode classes give B-1=(953616 sqrt(5)-4445)/6303442>0.
claims.source: Haapasalo, Compatibility of covariant quantum channels with emphasis on Weyl symmetry, arXiv:1901.06113, Corollary 2, Eq. (22).
claims.falsifier: A wrong class Fourier equation, compatibility-kernel phase convention, eigenvalue formula, or line assignment would invalidate the example; the five Fourier equations and exact formulas are reproduced in FINAL_REPORT.md and d5_exact_repair_audit.py.
claims.limitation: This disproves a universal line-cover budget bound B<=1, not the factor-two EB lift itself.

claims.statement: The exact d=5 channel in WCL-2 admits one factor-two EB comparator whose Choi state is an explicit convex mixture of Weyl-twirled product states.
claims.quantifiers: One common comparator for all 25 Weyl modes of this fixed channel.
claims.construction: Six exact-normalized rational complex kets, with six positive rational weights summing exactly to one; the comparator Choi state is their mixture of Weyl twirls of |psi><psi| tensor |conj(psi)><conj(psi)|. The input decimals are parsed as exact rational numbers and weights are renormalized exactly.
claims.check: 80-digit outward-rounded interval calculation certifies all 24 nonidentity mode inequalities. Minimum direct gap mu_x-(2 lambda_x-1) exceeds 0.0236367126398862; minimum clipped gap mu_x-(2 lambda_x-1)_+ exceeds 0.0139661206985528.
claims.limitation: The exact algebraic and interval checks have not been formalized in a proof assistant or independently reviewed. No separability witness for non-domination was obtained or needed; this comparator proves domination for this candidate.

claims.statement: The d=3 SCS search over all 81 active-mode selections returned maximum line-cover objective approximately 1.000000515, near the isotropic qutrit-cloner spectrum 5/8.
claims.quantifiers: The 81 line active-mode selections in the implemented optimization formulation, not a proof over the full feasible set.
claims.limitation: Not an analytic upper bound and not an exact solver certificate.

claims.statement: The d=5 example does not establish or refute the unrestricted operator-level factor-two EB domination conjecture or the bounded-Holevo approximate-broadcasting-to-one-common-EB-family implication.
claims.reason: The same d=5 channel has the explicit EB comparator in WCL-3; the calculation only falsifies the line-dephasing mixture route. A channel-specific comparator also does not meet a stronger state-family quantifier requiring one common reconstruction for an entire varying family.
